parsed.rationale: Although both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with `shared_field_count: 2` and no restraint markers, they carry distinct names — `PauseWXYC` in `Shared/Intents/Sources/Intents/PauseWXYC.swift` (package `Intents`) and `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` in `WXYC/iOS/Intents.swift` (package `app:iOS`) — which strongly suggests they alias different underlying SiriKit/App Intents types that happen to share the same structural shape. `PauseWXYC` encodes a pause action while `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` encodes a now-playing query; these are semantically unrelated intents whose coincidental structural equivalence does not warrant unification. Merging or aliasing them to a single declaration would conflate two distinct user-facing intent domains and could break intent routing. No safe refactor is available without more information about the underlying aliased types.
